name: Question 4
problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y,z)=z{x}^{2}+x{y}^{3}-y{z}^{4}.$
worked_solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $∇f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z{x}^{2}+x{y}^{3}-y{z}^{4}) \\  & =2xz+{y}^{3} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{x}^{2}+x{y}^{3}-y{z}^{4}) \\  & =3x{y}^{2}-{z}^{4} \\ {f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{x}^{2}+x{y}^{3}-y{z}^{4}) \\  & ={x}^{2}-4y{z}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =(2xz+{y}^{3})\,i+(3x{y}^{2}-{z}^{4})\,j+({x}^{2}-4y{z}^{3})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Find the gradient vector field of the function f(x,y,z)=zx2+xy3−yz4.

a
(2xz+y3)i+(6xy2+z4)j+(x−4yz3)k
b
(2xz+y2)i+(6xy−z4)j+(x2−8y3)k
c
(2xz+y3)i+(3xy2−z4)j+(x2−4yz3)k
d
(2x+y2)i+(3xy−z4)j+(x2−8yz2)k
e
(xz+y3)i+(3y2−z4)j+(x2−4z3)k
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The gradient vector field of a function f is given by ∇f.

First, we find the partial derivatives: fx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(zx2+xy3−yz4)=2xz+y3fy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(zx2+xy3−yz4)=3xy2−z4fz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(zx2+xy3−yz4)=x2−4yz3

Therefore, the gradient vector field of f(x,y,z) is ∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z)j+fz(x,y,z)k=(2xz+y3)i+(3xy2−z4)j+(x2−4yz3)k.
